findings.title: Condition panel is too dense to read while driving
findings.problem: The armour and tyre data is compressed into a narrow panel; armour faces are tiny square placeholders and tyre bars are thin, so damage state is not readable at a glance.
findings.why: During driving or combat, the player needs to know whether the car is failing without scanning a dense panel; tiny monochrome boxes feel like a debug readout.
findings.fix: Replace the armour rows with four large colored bars or segments labelled FRONT, REAR, LEFT, and RIGHT, use red/amber/green thresholds, and put tyre status in a wider horizontal strip.

findings.title: Constructor preview does not map parts to the car
findings.problem: The car preview is a small blue outline with two unlabeled rectangles, while the left list has many part rows; nothing shows which rectangle is selected or how armor and weapons attach.
findings.why: The build screen becomes a spreadsheet; players cannot read the consequences of selecting Body, Chassis, Armor, or Weapons.
findings.fix: Label the body, chassis, power-plant, weapon, and armor slots on the preview, highlight the selected row's slot, and show colored overlays for armor and weapon mounts.

findings.title: City yellow chevrons are visually noisy
findings.where: City, scattered around building entrances and road edges
findings.problem: Many identical yellow chevron barriers fill the map, including ones away from the car, so they compete with the cyan objective arrow and building entrances.
findings.why: At a glance, the player sees a field of roadwork signs rather than a destination; important interactions get buried in decorative clutter.
findings.fix: Reduce non-essential barriers, dim them to a neutral construction color, and reserve bright yellow or glowing markers for actual interactable entrances and objectives.

findings.title: Road progress bar is too abstract
findings.problem: The route indicator is a thin black line with a small white dot and no destination icon, mile markers, or filled progress.
findings.why: During courier driving, the player cannot quickly understand progress or direction; the bar feels like a debug slider rather than a readable navigation tool.
findings.fix: Add a destination chevron at the right end, a bright progress fill, mile markers every 25 miles, and a route arrow pointing toward Albany.

findings.title: Practice arena feels like an empty placeholder
findings.problem: The arena is a large featureless tiled floor with only the car, HUD, and a notification; there are no cover blocks, spawn points, obstacles, or enemy markers.
findings.why: The arena should communicate combat readiness, but this reads as a test map and weakens the fantasy of a vehicular combat space.
findings.fix: Add visible boundary lighting, cover blocks, spawn pads, enemy silhouettes or markers, and a few hazards or lane markings to give the space combat identity.
